# Convert Audio to M4A / AAC

- Route: `/tools/convert-audio-to-m4a`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `audio`
- Slug: `convert-audio-to-m4a`

## Summary

Turn MP3, M4A, WAV, OGG, FLAC and any other audio file into M4A / AAC at the bitrate you choose. (Audio tools)

## Details

M4A is AAC audio in an MP4 container, the format Apple Music, iPhones, YouTube and most streaming services use. It beats MP3 on quality per kilobyte. Media Manipulator converts any common audio format to M4A / AAC in one upload, keeping the sample rate and channel layout unless you change them, and offers trimming, normalisation, EQ and the AI cleanup tools on the same form.
### What it does
- Converts MP3, WAV, M4A/AAC, OGG, Opus, FLAC, ALAC, AC3 and WMA to M4A / AAC.
- Lets you pick the bitrate, sample rate and channel layout.
- Trim, gain, normalisation, EQ and effects go into the same encode as the AAC.
- AI tools on the form can clean a voice memo or remove vocals before the AAC is written.
### How to use it
1. Upload audio: A WAV master, an MP3 or a voice memo.
2. Adjust if needed: Pick the bitrate; trim or apply effects.
3. Convert: FFmpeg encodes M4A / AAC on our servers.
4. Download: Save the M4A / AAC file.
### Supported formats
- Input: mp3, wav, m4a, aac, ogg, opus, flac, alac, ac3, wma
- Output: aac
- Lossy output; the bitrate you choose sets the size.
### Technical details
- M4A / AAC output uses FFmpeg's aac encoder; 192 kbps is the default and a safe choice for music.
- Some older MP3-only players and car head units will not read AAC.
- An embedded album cover is recognised as a picture and never mistaken for a video track.
### Use cases
- Switch formats for a device: Make a M4A / AAC copy for a player that needs it.
- Prepare for editing: Make a small, compatible file for a project.
- One file at a time: Convert voice memos for an iPhone library, trimming dead air as you go.
- Clean up on the way: Run voice cleanup on a podcast take and save it straight to M4A.
### FAQ
Q: What is M4A / AAC?
A: M4A is AAC audio in an MP4 container, the format Apple Music, iPhones, YouTube and most streaming services use. It beats MP3 on quality per kilobyte.
Q: Will converting to M4A / AAC improve the sound?
A: No. Some older MP3-only players and car head units will not read AAC.
Q: Can I trim the audio while converting to M4A / AAC?
A: Yes. Set the range in the trim section; the M4A starts and ends where you said.
Q: Does the album art in my MP3 break the conversion to M4A?
A: No. The art stream is identified as a picture, not as video, and the AAC encode runs normally.
